foods.name: Homestyle Spinach & Onion Poha
foods.description: Fluffy flattened rice tempered with cumin, turmeric, green chili, diced potatoes, and fresh wilted spinach.
steps: Rinse poha in a colander until softened, then drain well.
Heat 1 tsp oil in a pan, temper cumin seeds, add finely chopped onions and diced potato.
Cover and cook on low heat until potato cubes are tender (about 6 minutes).
Add chopped spinach and turmeric powder; stir for 1 minute until wilted.
Fold in the softened poha, gently mix with salt to taste, and steam covered for 2 minutes.
foods.why_recommended: Uses potato, onion, and spinach from your pantry; ready in 15 minutes; well within morning ₹35 budget.

foods.name: Comforting Dal Tadka with Steamed Rice
foods.description: Hearty yellow lentils simmered with turmeric and garlic-free cumin-tomato tadka, served over fluffy steamed rice.
steps: Pressure cook dal with 1.5 cups water, turmeric, and salt for 3 whistles (or simmer 20 mins).
In another pot, steam the rice until fluffy.
Heat ghee in a small pan, add cumin seeds until fragrant, then saute onions until translucent.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook until soft and pulpy.
Pour the tempering into the boiled dal, bring to a gentle boil, and serve warm with rice.
foods.why_recommended: 100% pantry-aligned lunch; high protein from lentils; zero nut exposure; under ₹50 lunch target.

foods.name: Spiced Curd Dip with Roasted Cumin
foods.description: Cool, probiotic-rich fresh curd whipped with roasted cumin powder, mild black salt, and coriander.
steps: Whisk curd in a bowl until smooth and silky.
Sprinkle freshly roasted cumin powder, a pinch of black salt, and mild chili powder if desired.
Garnish with chopped fresh coriander and enjoy chilled.
foods.why_recommended: Instant 5-minute snack utilizing fresh curd from your pantry; refreshing, gut-healthy, and costs only ₹15.

foods.name: Savory Aloo Palak Sabzi with Phulka
foods.description: Tender golden potatoes stewed with a vibrant fresh spinach puree and mild Indian spices, paired with soft rotis.
steps: Blanch spinach leaves in boiling water for 2 minutes, then plunge in cold water and blend smooth.
Pan-sear diced potatoes in 1 tsp oil until light golden; set aside.
In the same pan, saute onions and tomato puree with ground coriander and mild turmeric.
Fold in the spinach gravy and potatoes; simmer on low heat for 8 minutes until potatoes are fork-tender.
Knead atta into dough, roll out thin phulkas, and puff over open flame.
foods.why_recommended: Uses potato, spinach, tomato, and onion from pantry; iron-rich; dinner cost ₹38 stays well within ₹45 cap.
